features.text: Patient is male and in his late 40s.
Left shoulder pain for approximately three weeks.
Left shoulder pain is constant and worsens with lifting or lying on the shoulder at night.
Left shoulder pain is described as a constant ache that becomes sharper with movement or pressure.
No numbness or weakness associated with the left shoulder pain.
No specific trauma or injury to the left shoulder in the past three weeks.
Patient has had previous shoulder aches and pains, but nothing serious.
Patient has noticed a limitation in the range of motion of the left arm.
Left shoulder pain worsens when reaching for objects or lifting, and the patient avoids reaching over the head.
No imaging studies or consultations with a healthcare provider for this shoulder pain.
Patient has been taking Tylenol to manage the pain.
No clicking, popping, or locking sensations in the left shoulder joint during movement.
No recent trauma or injury to the left shoulder, such as a fall or direct blow.
Patient has been doing a lot of work in the basement recently, which may have contributed to the onset of the pain.
No systemic symptoms such as fever, fatigue, weight loss, or morning stiffness in other joints.
No history of diabetes, thyroid disorders, or autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.
No imaging studies such as X-rays, MRI, or ultrasound of the left shoulder.
No radiation of pain to the arm, neck, or chest.
Patient has experienced shoulder stiffness and difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing or reaching behind the back.
